log.text: Toxic Spikes up on P1's side
Toxic Spikes up on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Blastoise. Lead Hippowdon and Blastoise: Hippowdon's Sand Stream immediately overwrites opposing Drought sun, while Mega Blastoise pressures Fire types (Charizard, Torkoal, Volcarona) with Water Spout and Aura Sphere. Sneasler and Whimsicott in back provide Fake Out disruption, Tailwind speed control, and Encore to clean up the endgame.
decisions.notebook: Opponent runs sun-heavy offense (Charizard-Y, Torkoal, Volcarona, Dragapult, Toxapex, Beedrill). Always prioritize resetting weather with Hippowdon's Sand Stream to neutralize sun multipliers on Fire attacks.

decisions.rationale: Mega Charizard Y + Torkoal guarantees Drought turn 1, outspeeding Sneasler/Whimsicott to threaten OHKOs with Heat Wave. Toxapex walls Water/Fairy types and disrupts with Toxic Spikes. Dragapult provides speed control and offensive pressure. This lead pressures fast threats while maintaining bulk and disruption.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's team relies on physical attackers (Sneasler, Mega Blastoise) and speed control (Whimsicott, Sneasler). Drought from Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal is critical to outspeed and overpower these threats. Toxapex is the primary counter to Water/Fairy types, while Dragapult ensures speed control and offensive presence. Avoid leading with Volcarona or Beedrill turn 1, as they are better suited for mid-game sweeps or cleanup. Watch for Hippowdon leads to disrupt Drought; Toxapex can absorb Earthquake hits and recover. Prioritize eliminating Sneasler and Whimsicott early to prevent Tailwind or Encore disruption.

decisions.rationale: Hippowdon uses Rock Slide to hit both Charizard (4x super-effective) and Torkoal (2x). Blastoise Mega Evolves and uses Water Spout to deal massive spread damage despite the sun, taking advantage of its high base stats and STAB.

Mega Evolving Charizard Y secures Drought permanently, outspeeding and threatening Blastoise with Heat Wave. Torkoal's Heat Wave pressures both foes under sun, risking minimal retaliation from Blastoise's Water Spout (0.5x). Protect is unnecessary turn 1 with no immediate KO threats.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's Hippowdon and Blastoise lead suggests a focus on spread damage and weather disruption. Prioritize Mega Charizard Y to lock in Drought and outspeed Sneasler/Whimsicott. Torkoal's Eruption is too risky turn 1 due to Blastoise's Water Spout resistance and Hippowdon's Earthquake. Toxapex is reserved for mid-game Water/Fairy control, while Dragapult handles late-game speed and cleanup. Watch for Whimsicott Tailwind or Sneasler FakeOut to disrupt sun-dependent strategies.

decisions.rationale: Torkoal is at 20% and Charizard-Y is at 56%. Blastoise-Mega's Water Spout cleanly finishes off both foes, and Hippowdon's Rock Slide provides insurance against Protect or chips them further.
Hippowdon fainted, so we must bring in Sneasler to replace it. Blastoise-Mega can fire off Water Spout to finish off the low-HP Charizard-Mega-Y and Torkoal, or pick up a quick KO through sun.

Solar Beam Hippowdon threatens KO after prior Rock Slide chip (58-69%). Torkoal Protect avoids Earthquake KO and scouts Blastoise. Prioritize removing Hippowdon to neuter Earthquake and Rock Slide spread pressure. Charizard outspeeds both foes to land Solar Beam before they act.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's Blastoise-Mega and Hippowdon lead confirms spread damage focus. Hippowdon's Rock Slide and Earthquake threaten Torkoal and Charizard respectively; removing Hippowdon first mitigates this. Blastoise's Water Spout and Ice Beam are secondary threats. Dragapult is reserved for late-game cleanup after sun weakens Water/Fairy types. Toxapex handles mid-game Fairy control. Sneasler and Whimsicott may attempt FakeOut or Tailwind disruption; maintain Protect and speed control to counter.

decisions.rationale: Charizard-Mega-Y is at 13% and Torkoal is at 20%. Sneasler's Dire Claw can KO Charizard-Mega-Y through potential Protect mindgames or afflict status, while Blastoise's spread Water Spout KOs both low-HP foes.

Sneasler outspeeds and threatens CloseCombat (27-49%) or FakeOut flinch; Blastoise Water Spout OHKOs Charizard from 14%. Protecting Charizard forces Blastoise to waste Water Spout or switch. Torkoal Earth Power OHKOs Sneasler if max invested, removing the immediate CloseCombat/FakeOut threat and securing a free turn for sun stalling or pivoting.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's Blastoise-Mega consistently targets Charizard with Water Spout, confirming Charizard as primary target. Sneasler's CloseCombat and FakeOut are secondary threats. Torkoal's Earth Power OHKOs Sneasler if max invested, making it a reliable removal tool. Prioritize Protect stalling on Charizard to force Blastoise into suboptimal moves or switches, while using Torkoal to eliminate Sneasler. Maintain sun to weaken Water Spout and Ice Beam. Dragapult is reserved for late-game cleanup after sun weakens Fairy/Water types. Toxapex handles mid-game Fairy control.

decisions.rationale: No valid decision (choices must be an array of exactly 2 integers); defaulted to the first legal option for each slot.

Charizard-Mega-Y is at 13% and used Protect last turn (success rate reduced). Sneasler outspeeds and can KO Charizard with Dire Claw or threaten Toxapex. Blastoise can use Water Spout to pressure both foes, especially since Charizard is very low and Toxapex resists water but takes heavy spread pressure. Sneasler acts first guaranteeing the pressure on Charizard.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Charizard at 14% cannot survive any Blastoise Water Spout or Sneasler CloseCombat. Protect stalls sun turns, forcing Blastoise into suboptimal moves or switches. Toxapex Recover maintains bulk for mid-game Fairy control. Air Slash/Surf risks Charizard KO without guaranteed Sneasler removal. Solar Beam is too slow vs. FakeOut priority.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise-Mega consistently targets Charizard with Water Spout, confirming it as primary threat. Sneasler's CloseCombat and FakeOut are secondary but lethal under sun. Sun weakens Water Spout and Ice Beam, but Charizard cannot survive another hit. Toxapex's Recover + Regenerator ensures longevity for mid-game Fairy control. Dragapult reserved for late-game cleanup after sun weakens Fairy/Water types. Prioritize Protect stalling to force opponent into unfavorable positions.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Sneasler targets Dragapult with Dire Claw (0.5x, but can poison if it stays or hits a switch) while Blastoise hits Toxapex with Ice Beam (Toxapex resists water/ice, but Ice Beam is our best neutral/coverage option). Alternatively, Sneasler hits Toxapex with Dire Claw. Let's use Sneasler Dire Claw on Dragapult and Blastoise Ice Beam on Toxapex.

Sun weakens Water Spout but Ice Beam OHKOes Dragapult. Thunder Wave cripples Sneasler's Speed, reducing immediate CloseCombat/Ice Beam threat. Recover sustains Toxapex for Toxic Spikes later. U-turn risks Dragapult to Blastoise-Mega's Ice Beam, while Draco Meteor wastes sun turns without disrupting Sneasler's Speed.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise-Mega prioritizes Water Spout on Charizard/Torkoal but shifts to Ice Beam for Dragapult under sun. Sneasler's CloseCombat is secondary but lethal; Thunder Wave mitigates its Speed advantage. Toxapex's Recover + Regenerator ensures longevity for mid-game Fairy control. Dragapult reserved for late-game cleanup after sun weakens Fairy/Water types. Toxic Spikes are critical for stalling Clefable/Whimsicott. Preserve Dragapult's Focus Sash for endgame.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex resists Water, Poison, and Fighting, and takes half damage from Water Spout. Bringing in Whimsicott via Sneasler's switch allows Encore or Tailwind setup against Toxapex, while Mega Blastoise keeps pressure with Water Spout.
decisions.notebook: Prioritize weather control and safe positioning against defensive pivots like Toxapex.

decisions.rationale: Toxic Spikes is the highest-leverage move, crippling Clefable/Whimsicott's setup and enabling stall with Regenerator + Recover. Protect risks are minimal due to Sneasler's paralysis and Blastoise's Water Spout PP reliance. Preserves Toxapex's longevity for endgame.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise-Mega prioritizes Water Spout PP conservation under sun, shifting to Ice Beam only for Dragapult. Sneasler's Close Combat is lethal but mitigated by paralysis; Toxic Spikes disrupts Clefable/Whimsicott setup. Toxapex's Recover + Regenerator ensures mid-game control. Dragapult reserved for late-game cleanup after sun weakens Fairy/Water types. Rotom's Choice Scarf and Whimsicott's Tailwind are critical for outspeeding Dragapult; plan to preserve Toxapex's bulk to counter them.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex just used Toxic Spikes last turn, making it prime fodder for Whimsicott's Encore. Blastoise can pressure with Water Spout while Toxapex is locked or forced to switch/struggle.

Recover sustains Toxapex under sun, punishes Whimsicott Protect, and prepares for Rotom/Whimsicott outspeed. Haze risks Blastoise PP, Toxic Spikes risks 2HKO. Prioritize bulk for late-game Dragapult cleanup.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise-Mega Water Spout PP conservation under sun is critical; avoid Haze unless Toxic Spikes are stacked. Toxapex Recover + Regenerator ensures mid-game control. Rotom's Choice Scarf and Whimsicott's Tailwind outspeed Dragapult; preserve Toxapex bulk to counter. Sneasler's Close Combat is lethal but mitigated by paralysis. Dragapult reserved for late-game cleanup after sun weakens Fairy/Water types.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex is encored into Surf on turn 7 and likely forced to use Surf again or Struggle/Recover depending on Encore timing. Blastoise-Mega can fire off Water Spout while Whimsicott uses Moonblast to chip away at Toxapex safely.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Toxapex is locked into Toxic Spikes via Encore on this turn (or it wears off and it's forced into another action, but Moonblast + Water Spout chips it down effectively since Water Spout is at low PP, wait, Water Spout has 1 PP left). Let's use Moonblast and Water Spout to finish off Toxapex while it is encored.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Toxapex lost Encore last turn and can use Recover or Toxic Spikes. We double into Toxapex to chip it down while Whimsicott uses Moonblast and Blastoise-Mega uses Ice Beam (or Water Spout is out of PP, so Ice Beam is best).

Recover maximizes Toxapex longevity under Toxic Spikes chip and Water Spout PP drain. Whimsicott Encore risks locking Toxapex into Surf/Toxic Spikes, but Recover is safe. Haze is premature without confirmed Rotom switch-in or Blastoise Sp. Atk drops. Preserve bulk to outlast Blastoise PP.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise-Mega Water Spout PP is finite; Toxapex Recover + Regenerator ensures mid-game control. Whimsicott Encore is high-risk for non-damaging moves; avoid Surf/Toxic Spikes unless Blastoise is weakened. Sneasler Close Combat is lethal but mitigated by paralysis. Rotom's Choice Scarf outspeeds Dragapult; Toxapex must preserve bulk to counter. Stack Toxic Spikes only after Blastoise PP is drained or sun is removed. Haze is reserved for emergency Toxic Spikes removal or Blastoise Sp. Atk drops.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott uses Moonblast and Blastoise-Mega uses Ice Beam on Toxapex to maintain offensive pressure and chip it down while its Recover is pressured.

Haze removes Toxic Spikes to deny opponent residual damage and resets Blastoise Sp. Atk drops, mitigating Water Spout pressure. Recover is less urgent with 85% HP and Leftovers/Regenerator. Toxic Spikes is too risky under Encore threat.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise Water Spout PP is finite (8/8 used); prioritize PP stall over Toxic Spikes stacking. Whimsicott Encore targets non-damaging moves aggressively; avoid Surf/Toxic Spikes unless Blastoise is weakened or locked. Haze is key for emergency Toxic Spikes removal or Blastoise Sp. Atk drop reset. Sneasler Close Combat is lethal but paralysis reduces its speed; maintain Toxapex bulk to counter. Rotom's Choice Scarf outspeeds Dragapult; Toxapex must preserve bulk to check Blastoise long-term. Sun is inactive; Torkoal/Charizard-Y are fainted and cannot re-establish weather.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex is currently frozen. Whimsicott uses Moonblast and Blastoise-Mega uses Ice Beam on Toxapex to continue wearing it down safely while keeping board control.

Haze is the safest play to reset Blastoise's Sp. Atk drops and remove Toxic Spikes, avoiding Encore lock. Protects Toxapex from further Sp. Atk pressure and preserves its role as Blastoise check. Recover is risky due to Encore, and Surf is weak vs. Blastoise's bulk.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise Water Spout PP is now 7/8; prioritize PP stall over Toxic Spikes stacking. Whimsicott Encore aggressively targets non-damaging moves; avoid Surf/Toxic Spikes unless Blastoise is locked or weakened. Haze remains critical for emergency Toxic Spikes removal and Blastoise Sp. Atk drop reset. Sneasler's Close Combat is lethal but paralysis reduces its speed; Toxapex must maintain bulk to counter. Rotom's Choice Scarf outspeeds Dragapult, but Toxapex is the primary Blastoise check. Sun is inactive and cannot be re-established.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex is currently frozen at 51% HP. Continuing to attack with Whimsicott's Moonblast and Blastoise-Mega's Ice Beam chips it down safely while ignoring its potential turns, maintaining total offensive pressure.

Haze is the only move that addresses both Toxic Spikes and Blastoise's SpA drop, critical for Toxapex's longevity. Encore risk is mitigated by Haze's utility, and Recover/Toxic Spikes are too risky under Encore pressure.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise Water Spout PP is now 7/8; PP stall remains a priority. Whimsicott's Encore targets non-damaging moves aggressively, so Haze must be used sparingly but decisively. Toxapex's bulk is sufficient to counter Blastoise if SpA drops are reset and Toxic Spikes are removed. Sneasler's Close Combat is lethal but paralysis reduces its threat; Toxapex must maintain HP to survive potential hits. Rotom's Choice Scarf outspeeds Dragapult, but Toxapex remains the primary Blastoise check. Future games: consider leading with a faster Toxic Spikes setter to avoid Encore pressure.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex is left at 33% HP after Haze. Whimsicott's Moonblast and Blastoise-Mega's Ice Beam apply simultaneous damage to break through its remaining HP and Leftovers recovery.
Recover sustains Toxapex to outlast Blastoise's Water Spout PP (7/8). Haze is risky under Encore; Surf is weak vs. both foes. Toxapex must survive to remove Toxic Spikes and counter Blastoise.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise Water Spout PP is now 7/8; PP stall is critical. Whimsicott Encore targets non-damaging moves, so Haze must be timed post-Encore. Toxapex's bulk is sufficient to counter Blastoise if SpA drops are reset and Toxic Spikes are removed. Future games: lead with a faster Toxic Spikes setter to avoid Encore pressure. Sneasler's Close Combat is lethal but paralysis reduces its threat; Toxapex must maintain HP to survive potential hits.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex just used Recover on turn 14, making Encore a high-probability way to lock it into Recover again and prevent Surf while Blastoise chips away with Ice Beam.

Haze resets Blastoise's SpA drops, enabling Toxapex to counter Water Spout PP stall. Recover sustains bulk to survive future hits, especially under Toxic Spikes. Encore risk is mitigated by Haze's immediate effect, and Toxapex's bulk ensures survival against Moonblast/Ice Beam.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise Water Spout PP is now 7/8; PP stall is critical. Whimsicott Encore targets non-damaging moves, so Haze must be timed to avoid lock. Toxapex's bulk is sufficient to counter Blastoise if SpA drops are reset and Toxic Spikes are removed. Future games: lead with a faster Toxic Spikes setter to avoid Encore pressure. Sneasler's Close Combat is lethal but paralysis reduces its threat; Toxapex must maintain HP to survive potential hits. Prioritize Toxic Spikes removal when Blastoise SpA is +0 to maximize counterplay.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex is locked into Recover by Encore for this turn. Whimsicott can attack with Moonblast and Blastoise-Mega can use Ice Beam into Toxapex to chip it down safely.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.
Toxapex is frozen and encored into Recover. Whimsicott uses Moonblast into Toxapex and Blastoise uses Ice Beam into Toxapex to chip it down while it remains locked and unable to act effectively.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.
Toxapex is frozen and weak to our continuous pressure, but we can also encore it if it wakes up. Continuing Moonblast and Ice Beam maintains damage output while preventing full recovery.
Haze resets Blastoise's SpA drops and removes Toxic Spikes, neutralizing PP stall. Encore risk is lower on Haze than Recover/Toxic Spikes. Toxapex's bulk and Leftovers sustain it for future turns.

Sneasler's Close Combat is lethal but paralysis reduces its threat; Toxapex must maintain HP to survive potential hits. Prioritize Toxic Spikes removal when Blastoise SpA is +0 to maximize counterplay.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex is the last remaining opponent and is weak to our sustained pressure despite resisting our attacks. We continue chipping it down with Moonblast and Ice Beam while it is low on HP.

Blastoise Water Spout PP is 7/8; PP stall is critical. Recover sustains Toxapex to outlast Blastoise after Haze resets SpA drops. Encore risk is lower on Recover than Haze/Surf. Toxapex must maintain HP to survive potential Sneasler Close Combat or Blastoise crits.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise Water Spout PP stall is the win condition; Toxapex must sustain HP to counter Blastoise after Haze resets SpA drops. Whimsicott Encore targets non-damaging moves, so Recover is safer than Haze/Surf. Future games: lead with a faster Toxic Spikes setter to avoid Encore pressure. Sneasler's Close Combat is lethal but paralysis reduces its threat; Toxapex must prioritize HP management to survive. Toxic Spikes removal is secondary to PP stall when Blastoise SpA is +0.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott uses Encore on Toxapex to lock it into its last move (likely Recover or Surf), while Blastoise uses Ice Beam to chip it down. Toxapex resists everything but Encore neutralizes its recovery/offense loop.
Blastoise Water Spout at +0 SpA cannot KO Toxapex after Recover (68% -> 100% HP). Encore risk is lower than Haze/Surf, as Whimsicott prefers Moonblast chip. PP stall remains viable.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise Water Spout PP stall is the win condition; Toxapex must prioritize HP sustain via Recover to survive +0 SpA Water Spout (68% -> 100% after Recover). Whimsicott Encore targets non-damaging moves, so Recover is safer than Haze/Surf. Future games: lead with a faster Toxic Spikes setter to avoid Encore pressure. Sneasler's Close Combat is non-threatening while paralyzed; Toxapex can ignore it. Toxic Spikes removal is secondary to PP stall when Blastoise SpA is +0.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex is encored into Recover. Whimsicott uses Moonblast and Blastoise-Mega uses Aura Sphere to slowly chip down Toxapex while it is locked into healing.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Whimsicott uses Encore on Toxapex to lock it into Recover or Surf, while Blastoise uses Aura Sphere to chip it down. Toxapex's Regenerator and Leftovers make chipping require locking it into Recover repeatedly.

Haze resets Blastoise's +0 SpA, neutralizing Water Spout's immediate threat. Recover next turn ensures Toxapex survives +0 Spout (68% -> 100%). Encore risk is lower on Haze than Recover, and Toxic Spikes are less urgent than PP stall.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise Water Spout PP stall remains the win condition; Toxapex must prioritize HP sustain via Recover to survive +0 SpA Water Spout (68% -> 100% after Recover). Whimsicott Encore targets non-damaging moves, making Haze safer than Recover when Blastoise's SpA is boosted. Future games: lead with a faster Toxic Spikes setter to avoid Encore pressure. Sneasler's Close Combat is non-threatening while paralyzed; Toxapex can ignore it unless paralysis wears off. Toxic Spikes removal is secondary to PP stall when Blastoise SpA is +0.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex just used Haze on turn 22, so it is free to use Encore on this turn. Encoring Toxapex locks it into Haze or whatever move it uses, while Mega Blastoise pressures it with Aura Sphere.

Haze resets Blastoise SpA boosts, preventing Water Spout OHKO after Recover. Encore cannot lock Toxapex into Haze, so PP stall remains viable. Surf/Toxic Spikes risk Encore locking into a move that either fails to chip or enables Water Spout KO.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise Water Spout PP stall is the win condition; Toxapex must prioritize Haze when Encore is active to reset SpA boosts and avoid Recover locks. Whimsicott Encore targets non-damaging moves, so Haze is safer than Recover or Toxic Spikes under Encore pressure. Future games: lead with a faster Toxic Spikes setter to avoid Encore pressure. Sneasler's Close Combat is non-threatening while paralyzed; Toxapex can ignore it unless paralysis wears off. Toxic Spikes removal is secondary to PP stall when Blastoise SpA is +0.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex is locked into Haze by Encore this turn. Continuing to attack with Moonblast and Aura Sphere chips Toxapex down safely while maintaining positioning.

Encore locks Toxapex into Haze or Recover, preventing it from effectively fighting back while Mega Blastoise chips it down with Aura Sphere.
Haze resets Blastoise SpA boosts, critical for Water Spout PP stall. Encore risk is high; Toxic Spikes/Surf are unsafe. Prioritize stall over chip.

Future games: lead with a faster Toxic Spikes setter to mitigate Encore pressure. Sneasler's Close Combat is non-threatening while paralyzed; Toxapex can ignore it unless paralysis wears off. Toxic Spikes removal is secondary to PP stall when Blastoise SpA is +0.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex is currently Encored into Haze, so it must use Haze again this turn. We can safely chip it down with Whimsicott's Moonblast and Blastoise's Mega Launcher-boosted Aura Sphere to finish off its remaining 17% HP without fear of offensive retaliation.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

reflections.summary: Mega Blastoise and Whimsicott successfully outlasted and broke down the defensive Toxapex in the endgame after the faster offensive threats were cleared.
reflections.adjustment: Retain the current team-preview structure, but ensure high-damage moves against Toxapex are preserved or PP-managed more efficiently to avoid protracted endgames.
reflections.notebook: Prioritize weather control and safe positioning against defensive pivots like Toxapex. Opponent uses Toxapex with Regenerator, Recover, Haze, and Toxic Spikes alongside Charizard-Y, Torkoal, and Dragapult.

reflections.summary: Lost due to inability to break Blastoise-Mega before Toxapex ran out of Recover PP and was overwhelmed by repeated Aura Sphere crits and Moonblast chip. Team-preview plan was flawed: Charizard-Y and Torkoal's Drought were redundant, while lacking a strong Water-type resist or offensive pressure to punish Blastoise's Protect stalling. Toxapex's Haze/Recover loop was out-PP'd by Blastoise's Aura Sphere spam, and Whimsicott's Encore forced predictable moves.
reflections.adjustment: Replace Torkoal with a Water-resistant Pokémon (e.g., Gastrodon) to absorb Water Spout and threaten Blastoise. Adjust lead to Dragapult + Toxapex to apply early pressure and avoid double Drought redundancy. Prioritize Toxic Spikes removal earlier to reduce Blastoise's PP advantage.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tendencies: Blastoise-Mega relies on Aura Sphere PP stall (16 PP) after Water Spout depletes; Whimsicott uses Encore to lock Toxapex into Haze/Recover. Strategic facts: Blastoise's Modest nature and Mega SpA investment make it difficult to tank even resisted hits; Sneasler's paralysis is irrelevant if Toxapex is the focus. Future plans: Avoid double Drought leads; bring a Water resist to punish Blastoise's Protect stalling. Test Gastrodon or Amoonguss to disrupt Blastoise's PP cycle. Toxapex must Haze early to prevent Blastoise from snowballing SpA boosts.
